Original review- Awesome camera, so far printer is working great and quickly. Touch screen is great, pictures were a little smaller than i expected them to be, but that's a researching error on my part. I love the filter and options to make the photo look like the old polaroid photos. I love the option to print certain photos so you're just not wasting film, and that you can print multiple copies of the same image. The battery life is also nice. All around, if you're looking for a polaroid camera, with more options than just shoot and print, this is a great choice.

I had to send this unit back because it did not communicate with my Samsung 65" TV. It kept blinking on and off. Annoying and unacceptable. The Sony 800 4K Blu-ray player works, but only on the TV's input #3. Go figure.

I think I'm going to steer clear of Samsung electronic devices.

Two reviews for products on this page: TL-SG2008P, TL-SG2210MP:
(whoever sells this junk needs to split the page for each product)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
TL-SG2008P:
Comes in two parts: switch + power brick.

There is no way to set the power limits on each of the lines.
There is no way to disable poe on a single line, e.g. to reboot a device.

Looks like TP-Link saved $8 on relays and voltage meters *faceslap*

All the stats are aggregated in the UI under port 1.
If port 1 is disabled, all poe ports are disabled.

The budged for the poe 1 line is 30W, but since it counts all other lines,
the whole device budget is just 30W - and not 63W.

Otherwise it works OK but then any other unmanaged POE switch for $30 would do.

Boots in about a minute :-O

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
TL-SG2210MP:
Comes in one piece. The switch has the power-brick integrated. Which is nice.
Looks pro, meaning it does not look like a cheapened version like above.
There are 4 x solid state relays, so possibly each PoE channel is managed.
Did not tested it because...

once plugged in it gave terrible noise from the integrated fan.
Only usable in a rack in the basement or network closet.
Not for home customers.

Boots in about a minute :-O make sure to put it on UPS.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

I wanted to love this. I love Sony and the reviews on this were excellent. First off the sound is very good. When I first tested it I was wowed as it was so much better than the earbuds from Apple (the ones that had the mic attached--the old style ones that are round and not shaped to first in ears). I bought these because (1) I wanted earbuds that stayed in my ear better (2) I wanted them not to have a mic because I also wanted them to work with my old shuffle (3) I wanted a little better quality--I mostly use them for podcasts and not music so they didn't have to be excellent.

So, as I said the sound was remarkably better and they fit wonderfully in my ears. I don't know durability because I've only had them for less than a week so I can't comment on that. Here's the one bad thing but it's so annoying that I dropped it two stars. I use them mostly when I exercise. So I walk a track or hike a hill. These mics pick up a vibration from the cord as you're moving. So if you're not moving they are wonderful but moving...annoying. I have to wrap the cord over my ears or hold it in my hand and try not be get it move at all. Otherwise I hear a bit of 'klunk klunk klunk.' I would not buy these again and am thinking of returning them as I do the majority of my listening while exercising. If you do the same I would look elsewhere.
